q1_what_did_you_play: I played Fwoosh! into the Shrinker Beetle and then Kaboom! into it, for 15 damage total, and I stopped there. The beetle sits at 30 HP and there is no arrangement of this hand that kills it, so the turn is just about squeezing out the most damage I can without paying for anything I do not need. Fwoosh! is free in energy and costs one of my two Sparks for 8 damage; Kaboom! costs one of my three energy for 7. That leaves me two unspent energy and one unspent Spark, and I could not find anything worth doing with either. I deliberately did not play Duck and Cover: the beetle's telegraph says it is applying a debuff, not swinging, so 5 Block would sit there and expire without ever touching anything. Playing it would have looked like a turn with more actions in it, but it would have bought me exactly nothing.
q2_other_line_considered: The only thing I actually weighed was Dodoco Blast, and it fell apart the moment I did the arithmetic. It wants both of my Sparks and pays 7 damage to everything on the board — but there is only one thing on the board, so the 'ALL enemies' clause is worth nothing here, and 7 is less than the 8 Fwoosh! gives me for half the Spark cost. It is strictly worse in every column that matters on this board. After spending on Fwoosh! I am down to one Spark, so Dodoco Blast is not even castable as a follow-up; the two Spark cards are mutually exclusive and one of them is plainly dominated. I also briefly considered whether holding the second Spark for a future turn was a real consideration, but since nothing in this hand can bank or spend it further this turn, holding it is what happens by default rather than a choice I made. Honestly, this turn did not present me with a decision — it presented me with a sum.
q3_what_it_gave_up: In concrete terms I gave up the 5 Block from Duck and Cover, one Spark, and two energy, and I do not think any of the three was worth having. The Block is the only one that could theoretically matter, and it only matters if I have misread the beetle or if it does something on its turn that the printed intent does not tell me about — that is the real risk I took, trusting the telegraph. I also gave up the AoE tag on Dodoco Blast, which is meaningless against a single target but would be the thing I regret if the fight were about to add bodies. The other cost is tempo-shaped rather than immediate: I emptied my Spark bank down to 1 to squeeze out one extra point of damage over the Dodoco line, so if next turn hands me something that wants two Sparks I will not have them. Against a 30 HP enemy where I am chipping 15 a turn, I judged the point of damage now was worth more than the option later.
q4_different_intent: Yes, though only at the margin. If the beetle were telegraphing an attack of any real size, Duck and Cover goes from dead card to obvious inclusion — I have three energy and Kaboom! only wants one, so I would play both and end the turn with 5 Block up rather than leaving energy on the table. The two attacks would not change: Fwoosh! and Kaboom! are still the best damage available regardless of what the enemy is doing, and Dodoco Blast stays dominated no matter the intent, because the intent does not change how many enemies there are. So the attacking half of my line is intent-proof and the defensive half is entirely intent-driven. An intent that added a second enemy — a summon, say — would be the one thing that could genuinely flip the Spark decision toward Dodoco Blast, but a debuff telegraph is not that.
